title: SCAFFOLD: Stochastic Controlled Averaging for Federated Learning
layout_note: A parameter-space sketch: two clients' local SGD trajectories drawn as chains of dots diverging from a common start, the server's averaged point between them, the client optima and true optimum as square markers on the right, and a legend column at the far right.
grouping: No containers. Meaning is carried by marker colour and arrow colour, keyed in a right-hand legend column (client update, server update, SGD update, client drift, true opt., client opt.). Client 1's path runs up, client 2's down; labels sit at the ends of each path.
shapes_depth: Flat vector sketch: iterates are filled circles (dark grey start and server point, blue client iterates, pale grey intermediate averages); optima are small squares (blue true optimum, orange client optima) joined by a dashed line. Arrows are thin and colour-coded (blue client steps, green server steps, black drift); small white squares mark the centralised SGD reference steps. Bold italic math labels (x, y_1, x*_1).
proposed_highlight: No method is shown; the figure isolates the problem the paper fixes - the averaged server point lands away from the true optimum because client paths drift toward their own optima (orange squares).
lesson: Show heterogeneity as geometry: draw each client's local steps as a dot chain bending toward its own optimum marker and the server point as their average, so client drift is visible without a single equation.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF footer (Proceedings of the 37th ICML, PMLR 119, 2020).

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
